content: 1. The HIV Care and Treatment Patient Card is a comprehensive tool designed to document and monitor the care and treatment of individuals living with HIV. It includes detailed information about antiretroviral therapy (ART) initiation, transfer, and regimen history. 2. The card records the date of ART initiation, the specific first-line regimen used, and any prior antiretroviral (ARV) medications taken, including during pregnancy or breastfeeding. It also tracks ARV prophylaxis for HIV-exposed infants and any interruptions in ART treatment. 3. Family status is documented, including the relationship to the patient, HIV status of family members, and unique identifiers. If applicable, the date of death is recorded. 4. The card captures the patient’s HIV testing history, including the date of the first positive test, confirmation of HIV diagnosis, and any virological or antibody tests performed. It also notes the location of testing and enrollment into HIV care. 5. Drug allergies, chronic conditions, and concomitant medications are recorded. Tuberculosis (TB) status is assessed at each visit, with details on TB therapy, symptoms, investigations, and treatment outcomes. 6. For HIV-exposed infants, follow-up information is documented, including prophylaxis, HIV testing, and final status (e.g., positive, negative, or unknown). Nutritional support and infant feeding practices are also noted. 7. ART treatment interruptions, including missed drug pick-ups, reasons for stopping, and dates of restart, are tracked. Follow-up status, including loss to follow-up, transfer out, or death, is recorded. 8. The card includes baseline demographic information such as date of birth, age, sex, marital status, address, and contact details. It also identifies treatment supporters and home-based care providers. 9. Patient progress is monitored through follow-up visits, with weight, height, and other clinical parameters recorded. For children, additional metrics such as mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) and vaccination status are included. 10. Pregnancy and reproductive health (RH) choices are documented, including pregnancy status, family planning methods, and any history of abortion or miscarriage. Codes are used to specify reproductive intentions and contraceptive methods. 11. Comorbidities and coinfections, including opportunistic infections (OIs), sexually transmitted infections (STIs), and major non-communicable diseases (NCDs), are recorded. For children, nutritional problems and growth issues are noted. 12. Treatment-limiting toxicities and adverse reactions are documented, including gastrointestinal, skin, neurological, hepatic, hematological, and metabolic side effects. Specific codes are used to classify these toxicities. 13. TB status is assessed at every visit, with symptoms suggestive of TB (e.g., cough, fever, night sweats, weight loss) prompting further investigation. TB treatment and preventive therapy are recorded, along with specimen test results and outcomes. 14. Hepatitis screening and vaccination are included. If hepatitis B or C is diagnosed, liver disease staging and treatment are documented. Testing of partners and children is also recommended. 15. Reasons for non-adherence to ART are categorized, including forgetfulness, side effects, stigma, financial constraints, and other barriers. Missed doses and their causes are recorded. 16. Nutritional support and counseling are provided, with specific guidance for infant feeding practices. Therapeutic feeding and food support are documented as needed. 17. ART investigations, including CD4 count, viral load, hemoglobin, and other relevant tests, are recorded. Results are linked to specific visit dates for continuity of care. 18. Codes are used to classify TB specimen test results, ART regimen changes, and reasons for substitution, switching, or stopping treatment. These codes ensure standardized documentation and facilitate clinical decision-making. 19. Vaccination history for children is recorded, including vaccines such as BCG, hepatitis B, polio, measles, and others. Additional vaccines may be documented based on regional guidelines. 20. Education on HIV basics, prevention, disclosure, and ART preparation is emphasized. Patients are supported in understanding their treatment and managing their condition effectively.
